The story demonstrates a strong sense of unity where all the elements—setting, imagery, and character actions—interweave seamlessly to create a cohesive and haunting whole. The rising floodwaters in the beginning not only establish an eerie, impending atmosphere, but also serve a literal plot function later when the current carries the burned chair down the street to the narrator. Furthermore, the unsettling imagery of the burned armchair is carefully echoed in the description of the woman inside the apartment (her soaked coat blending into the chair, her "stiff black tufts" of hair resembling the coiled springs, and her silhouette appearing as a "dense blackness, crackled where the light caught it"). Finally, the gesture of the woman laying her palm flat on the ruined chair in the beginning is mirrored by the man laying his palm on her shoulder in the middle, and the narrator reaching out a hand at the end, binding the beginning, middle, and end into a deeply unified, surreal narrative.
